chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Khums is not [obligatory] except in the war booty specifically.'

Thus, what is meant is that Khums is not [obligatory by] the apparent meaning of the Quran except in the war booty specifically, because whatever is apart from the war booty in which we have obligated Khums, that is established entirely by the Sunnah, and the Imam (peace be upon him) did not mean that Khums is not obligatory in it under any circumstance.
ai.seo_question: Is Khums only for war booty according to the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the Quran explicitly mandates Khums only on war booty (al-ghanaim), the obligation for other wealth categories is firmly established through the Sunnah, preventing the misconception that non-mentioned assets are exempt. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Sunnah serves as a complementary source of legislation, expanding the scope of divine obligations beyond the literal text of the Quran. The narration thus reinforces the authority of the Imams in interpreting and applying religious duties to contemporary economic contexts.
